Man Buys New 2014 SRT Viper GTS for $134,080, Drives 799 Miles, Sells for $183,000
38 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer/autoevolution
Had to do a bit of math for this one, but according to the numbers, the value on this car went up by just over $61 for every mile that it’s been driven. And it hasn’t been driven that much. The original owner put just 799 miles on the odometer before deciding to auction it off.
The car retailed for $134,080 back when SRT was its own brand, and just yesterday it sold for a whopping $183,000. The value shot up by 36.5% on a car that sold rather poorly, originally. You guys remember how much Dodge/SRT struggled with fifth-gen Viper sales, right? Sales were so poor that production had to be cut and paused, at one point.
Overall, the fifth-gen Viper was by far the lowest-selling generation in the nameplate’s history, which led directly to its discontinuation. This had such an effect on Dodge that they never even considered coming up with an all-new model. I guess when you’re doing so well with your Hellcat-powered Challengers and Chargers, you’d rather not rock the boat too much.
But now that we’ve entered the era of electrification, I can totally see the Viper coming back in whatever capacity. Personally, I think there’s a place for it in the combustion engine supercar segment, but an EV would work too, I guess – it’s better than nothing. Ideally though, I’d like to see an all-new Viper taking the fight to the C8 Corvette . That would be spectacular.
And yes, they should go ahead and make it rear mid-engined. It worked for the Corvette and it should work for the Viper too. That’s the category supercars need to attack nowadays. Otherwise, who are you going to challenge with a front-engine supercar? The 12Cilindri and the Vanquish? The AMG-GT? I think not.
In terms of specs, aside from its Gunmetal Pearl colorway, this Viper GTS also comes with dual black racing stripes, xenon headlights, a GTS-specific vented hood, a rearview camera, integrated rear spoiler, dual side exhaust outlets, plus a set of black 18” and 19” Venom alloy wheels rocking staggered-width Pirelli P Zero rubber and red Viper-branded Brembo calipers over vented rotors.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Interior highlights include the black Nappa leather and Alcantara Sabelt bucket seats, a 12-speaker sound system, power-adjustable pedals, automatic climate control, cruise control, sat-nav, and a leather-wrapped steering wheel.
As for the engine, it’s a massive… and I do mean massive 8.4-liter V10 of the hand-assembled variety, pushing out 640 horsepower and 600 lb-ft of torque. Everything gets sent to the rear wheels via a Tremec six-speed manual gearbox.
Getting all that power down can be a struggle, but if you hook properly, you should be able to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill in about 3.5 seconds. Meanwhile, the top speed is 206 mph (332 kph).
